text: The B.S. in Computer Engineering degree plan (2022-2023 Catalog) requires 126 total hours for graduation, which must include a minimum of 51 hours as Upper Division. The plan totals 71 lower-division hours and 55 upper-division hours: Major Preparatory Requirements (43 lower-division hours, included in Major GPA); Major Core Requirements (55 upper-division hours, included in Major GPA); Remaining Core Curriculum (24 lower-division hours); and Electives (0 hours with Math 2413 credit, 4 hours with Math 2417 credit). Students must have a minimum cumulative 2.0 GPA in all UTD coursework and a cumulative 2.0 GPA in all Major requirements to graduate. Students must also complete 45 hours in residence and complete 24 of the last 30 hours at UTD. No off-campus coursework in the last semester is allowed.
source_title: B.S. in Computer Engineering Degree Plan (2022-2023 Catalog)
section_heading: B.S. in Computer Engineering: Degree Totals and Graduation Requirements

text: B.S. in Computer Engineering (2022-2023 Catalog) degree plan notes: (1) Major requirement; must earn C- or better to receive credit. (2) Must earn a C or better to receive credit. (3) Course meets both Major and CORE requirement. (4) Incoming freshmen (FTIC) must enroll and complete requirements of UNIV 1010 and the corresponding school-related freshmen seminar course; transfer students may be required to complete an additional upper level (3000 or 4000) CE course substitution. (5) All students, including transfer students, who complete their core curriculum at UT Dallas must take UNIV 2020. (6) Most lower division (LD) coursework can be taken at a community college and transferred; see the online transfer plan for course equivalents. Courses in the Major Preparatory Requirements and Major Core Requirements are included in the Major GPA.

text: B.S. in Computer Engineering (2022-2023 Catalog) Major Preparatory Requirements (43 lower-division hours), engineering and computing courses: ECS 1100 Intro to Engineering and CS (1 hour); CE 1100 Intro to Electrical and Computer Engineering (1 hour); CE 1202 Intro to Computer Engineering II (2 hours); CS 1336 Programming Fundamentals (3 hours); CS 1136 Computer Science Laboratory (1 hour); CE 1337 Computer Science I (3 hours); CE 2336 or 2337 Computer Science II (3 hours); CE 2310 Introduction to Digital Systems (3 hours); CE 2305 Discrete Mathematics for Computing I (3 hours); and ENGR 2300 Linear Algebra for Engineers (3 hours). ECS 1100, CE 1100, CE 1202, CE 2310, and ENGR 2300 are major requirements requiring C- or better, with ECS 1100 and CE 1100 tied to the FTIC freshman seminar requirement. CS 1336, CE 1337, CE 2336/2337, and CE 2305 require a C or better. Most lower division coursework, including the Major Preparatory courses, can be taken at a community college and transferred; see the online transfer plan for course equivalents.
source_title: B.S. in Computer Engineering Degree Plan (2022-2023 Catalog)

text: B.S. in Computer Engineering (2022-2023 Catalog) Major Preparatory Requirements, mathematics and physics courses: MATH 2414 Integral Calculus or MATH 2417 Calculus I (4 hours); MATH 2415 Calculus of Several Variables or MATH 2419 Calculus II (4 hours); MATH 2420 Differential Equations w/ Applications (4 hours); PHYS 2325 Mechanics (3 hours); PHYS 2125 Physics Laboratory I (1 hour); PHYS 2326 Electromagnetism and Waves (3 hours); and PHYS 2126 Physics Laboratory II (1 hour). All are major requirements requiring C- or better. The two calculus courses, PHYS 2325, PHYS 2125, and PHYS 2326 also meet a CORE requirement. The Major Preparatory Requirements total 43 lower-division hours.

text: B.S. in Computer Engineering (2022-2023 Catalog) Major Core Requirements (55 upper-division hours total), part 1: CE 3161 Social Issues and Ethics in Engineering (1 hour); CE 3201 CE Fundamentals Lab I (2 hours); CE 3202 CE Fundamentals Lab II (2 hours); CE Elective Lab (2 hours; see the list of options); CE 3301 Electrical Network Analysis (3 hours); CE 3303 Discrete-Time Signals and Systems (3 hours); CE 3311 Electronic Circuits (3 hours); CE 3320 Digital Circuits (3 hours); ENGR 3341 Probability Theory & Statistics (3 hours); and CE 3345 Data Structures & Intro to Algorithmic Analysis (3 hours). All are major requirements; a grade of C- or better is required to receive credit.

text: B.S. in Computer Engineering (2022-2023 Catalog) Major Core Requirements (55 upper-division hours total), part 2: CE 3354 Software Engineering (3 hours); CE 4304 Computer Architecture (3 hours); CE 4348 Operating Systems Concepts (3 hours); CE 4370 Embedded Systems (3 hours); CE 4388 Senior Design Project I (3 hours); CE 4389 Senior Design Project II (3 hours); three CE Guided Electives (3 hours each, 9 hours total; see the list of options); and ECS 3390 Professional & Technical Communication (3 hours; also meets a CORE requirement).
